parameter.name: container
parameter.description: The container the blob is written to.

parameter.name: blob
parameter.description: The blob name, including any virtual directory prefix.

parameter.name: blockSize
parameter.description: Block size, e.g. 32MB. Omit to derive one from the source size. This sets the largest blob that can be written: Azure allows 50,000 blocks, so 4MB caps the blob at 195GB and 32MB at 1.53TB.

parameter.name: blockSizeUnit
parameter.description: Unit for blockSize: B, KB, MB or GB. Defaults to B, so a bare blockSize is a plain byte count.

parameter.name: overwrite
parameter.description: false to fail rather than replace an existing blob. Defaults to true.

parameter.name: uploadConcurrency
parameter.description: Blocks staged at once, 1-256, default 4. The pool holds blockSize x uploadConcurrency bytes of heap for the whole transfer, and only a combination larger than the entire heap is refused. 1 makes the upload sequential.

parameter.name: checkpointFrequency
parameter.description: Blocks between checkpoints, default 1. At most this many blocks are re-uploaded after a failure. A staged block is invisible until the blob is committed and re-staging the same block is idempotent, so raising it costs only bandwidth on a resume - never a repeated side effect - and buys one fewer fsync per block.

parameter.name: verifyBlocks
parameter.description: false to skip the per-block MD5. On by default: Azure compares the hash against what arrived and rejects a corrupted block with 400, so the failure is a retry rather than a silently wrong blob.
